title: Governing equations in coordinates, boundary conditions and kinds of flow
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Publisher-uploaded English captions (NPTEL YouTube channel, non-automatic track)
source_uncertainties: The publisher captions' title cards say Week 04 Lecture 13 (rkkohAdwBR4) and Week 05 Lecture 14 (NEsucCXr5GA); manifest/YouTube course labels are Lecture 11 and Lecture 12. Heading labels follow the manifest.
All source videos were deliberately deleted before drafting. Read complete publisher transcripts and scanned 5+6 contact sheets; only retained frames were viewed. No video-viewing claim is made.

L11 cylindrical curl determinant (f0059, f0064) is written with factors on basis vectors and unweighted Vr,Vtheta,Vz below. Read literally as a Cartesian determinant it omits the derivative of rVtheta. The chapter derives components from circulation, supplies the standard weighted determinant and checks rigid rotation omega_z=2Omega.

L11 radial viscous derivative f0067 and theta derivative f0075 use d/dr[(1/r)d(rV_component)/dr]. The chapter expands this to scalar Laplacian minus V_component/r^2; these are equivalent, not source corrections.

L12 f0058/f0061 displays p1-2mu1*dV1y/dy = p2-mu2*dV2y/dy (missing the second factor 2). Earlier stress matrix f0047/f0053 contains both diagonal 2mu terms. Chapter Eq. (6.25) keeps factor 2 on both sides, derived from the matrix.

L12 captions/board describe Vy=0 as following from a horizontal interface. The chapter additionally requires stationarity and no mass transfer; a translating horizontal interface has nonzero normal speed.

L12 free-surface reduction f0075 writes a derivative with x where the developed shear condition requires y; Eq. (6.26) and its free-surface limit use the normal derivative dVx/dy, derived from total stress.

L12 speech suggests surface tension implies a curved rather than horizontal interface. Chapter distinguishes zero curvature pressure jump for a flat interface from possible tangential surface-tension-gradient forces.
Far-field explanation separates laboratory and translating body frames consistently; finite energy is motivation, not a proof of all pointwise decay.

Thompson-Troian author-hosted PDF pp.360-361 was available via web PDF text with explicit page mapping. Direct Python download returned HTTP403; no local PDF copy was obtained. Its claims are page-text checked, not based on unseen figures.

Brackbill-Kothe-Zemach PDF pp.336-338 was downloaded and rendered; its normal points into fluid2 with curvature positive toward that phase. The chapter explicitly defines its own outward-from-fluid1 sphere convention and checks the sign by a hemisphere force balance.

All liquid density/viscosity, optional sound speed and optional surface tension in the running case are constructed inputs, not sourced measured values. No universal Reynolds-number transition or Mach cutoff is asserted.
Passes 7 and 8 completed by the round-1 fixer. Independent gate 6b round 2 and lead pass 9/build/browser validation remain; no acceptance is claimed.
